OMRON opens LD-150 and LD-300 orders ahead of January deliveries

The new mobile robots carry 150 or 300 kg and integrate with existing fleets through FLOW Core.

OMRON Robotics ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 10Videos 1

The new development

OMRON has opened orders for its LD-150 and LD-300 autonomous mobile robots in the Americas and Europe, with deliveries scheduled to begin in January 2027 subject to country-specific approvals. The milestone is order availability; it does not mean deliveries have already started in every market.

Technology and applications

The LD-150 carries 150 kg and measures 500 mm wide, while the LD-300 carries 300 kg and measures 580 mm wide. OMRON specifies operation in one-metre aisles, speeds up to 2.1 metres per second and slopes up to five degrees. Application-specific top modules support different material-handling tasks.

Scope and next steps

FLOW Core coordinates routes, jobs and traffic alongside LD, MD, OL and HD robots, supporting fleets of up to 100 units. OMRON states an 18-minute wireless charging time. Facilities still need to assess payloads, routes and accessories for their own processes; this announcement does not establish a Thai availability date.
